record.title: Existence of scattering limits for the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation
record.statement:
For the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ defined on page 45, with $d>1$, the report states that
\[
\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}\Phi^{-t}\varphi_t(u)=:u_\pm=\Omega_\pm(u)
\]
exists in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/34](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11126), page 47. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Existence of a small even large-image Galois representation
record.statement: Does there exist a prime $p<1{,}000{,}000$ and an even representation $\rho:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$, unramified outside $p$, whose image contains $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/35](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11127), page 15. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Rational points on non-split Cartan modular curves
record.statement:
Does there exist a constant $c$ such that, for every prime number $p>c$, the only $
Q$-points of the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}(p)$ over $
Q$ are CM points? Here $X_{\mathrm{ns}}(n)$ is the quotient of the full-level modular curve $X(n)$ by the normalizer $C_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(n)$ of a non-split Cartan subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/35](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11127), page 34. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Algorithm for enumerating relative cubic extensions over imaginary quadratic fields
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic number field with class number $h_K=1$. For $X>0$, let
\[
\mathcal F_{K,3}(X)=\{\text{isomorphism classes of extensions }L/K:[L:K]=3,\ \mathcal N_{K/\mathbb Q}(\mathfrak d(L/K))\le X\}.
\]
There exists an algorithm that lists all cubic extensions in $\mathcal F_{K,3}(X)$ in time $O_{\varepsilon}(X^{1+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/35](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11127), page 43. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Maximal Riesz-transform boundedness versus variational boundedness
record.statement: Given an arbitrary nonatomic measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), does boundedness of the maximal Riesz transform \(R_*^\mu\) on \(L^2(\mu)\) imply boundedness of \(\mathcal{V}_\rho\circ R^\mu\) on \(L^2(\mu)\), for \(\rho>2\)?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/36](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11128), page 8. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Semiregular automorphisms of finite vertex-transitive graphs
record.statement: Does every finite vertex-transitive graph have a semiregular automorphism, that is, an automorphism whose cycles all have the same length $\ll>1$?

record.title: Existence of an extremal binary code of length 72

record.title: Higman’s PORC conjecture
record.statement: For each fixed $n$, let $f_n(p)$ denote the number of groups of order $p^n$, where $p$ ranges over the primes. Higman’s conjecture is that $f_n(p)$ is polynomial on residue classes (PORC): there exist polynomials $g_1(p),\ldots,g_k(p)$ and a positive integer $N$ such that, for every prime $p$, $f_n(p)=g_i(p)$ for some $i$, with the choice of $i$ depending only on the residue class of $p\pmod N$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/37](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11129), page 20. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: PORC behavior of the number of groups of order $p^{10}$
record.statement: Is the total number of groups of order $p^{10}$, as a function of the prime $p$, a PORC function?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/37](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11129), page 21. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Gal’s conjecture for flag simple polytopes
record.statement: **Conjecture 1 (Gal, 2005).** Any flag simple $n$-polytope $P$ satisfies $\\gamma_i(P^n) \\ge 0$ for $i=0,\\ldots,\\left\\lfloor n/2\\right\\rfloor$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/41](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11133), page 19. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Strong universal consistency in static forecasting under mere integrability
record.statement:
Does there exist a sequence of static forecasting estimates $m_n(X_0,D_{-1}^{-n})$ such that, for every stationary and ergodic sequence $((X_n,Y_n))_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ of $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R$-valued random variables satisfying $\mathbb E|Y_0|<\infty$, one has
\[
m_n(X_0,D_{-1}^{-n})\longrightarrow \mathbb E\!\left[Y_0\mid X_{-\infty}^{0},Y_{-\infty}^{-1}\right]\quad\text{almost surely}?
\]
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/42](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11134), page 27. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Theta-function norm bounds for general groups and lattices
record.statement: For what groups $G$ and lattices $\Gamma$ can one prove such bounds for all theta functions?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/43](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11135), page 22. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Sup-norm bound for Hecke–Maass newforms of square-free level
record.statement:
Let $f$ be an $L^2$-normalized Hecke–Maass cuspidal newform of square-free level $N$, with trivial nebentypus and Laplacian eigenvalue $\$. Prove that, for every $\>0$,

$$\ f\_\\infty\ \ll_{\,\u001b} N^{-1/6+\},$$

where the implied constant depends continuously on $\$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/43](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11135), page 34. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Lindelöf hypothesis for the Riemann zeta-function
record.statement: For every \4\varepsilon>0\4, \(\zeta(\tfrac12+it)\ll t^{\varepsilon}\) as \(t\to\infty\).
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/43](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11135), page 50. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Purdy’s conjecture on planes versus lines determined by points in 3-space
record.statement: For all sufficiently large $n$, let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in $3$-space such that the points do not all lie on two skew lines and no plane contains $n-1$ of the points. If $p$ is the number of planes determined by $P$ and $l$ is the number of lines determined by $P$, then $p\ge l$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11136), page 14. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Algorithmic undecidability of topological $d$-representability
record.statement: For every fixed integer $d\ge 5$, it is algorithmically undecidable, given a finite simplicial complex $K$ abstractly as a collection of faces, whether $K$ is topologically $d$-representable; that is, whether $K$ is isomorphic to the nerve of a finite good cover of open sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where every nonempty subcollection has intersection either empty or contractible.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11136), page 23. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Circle-freeness of Minkowski sums with a ball
record.statement: Is it true that for every circle-free convex body $K$, the set $K+B$ is also circle-free?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11136), page 40. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Crossing-number lower bound for arbitrary drawings of complete graphs
record.statement:
For every integer $n\ge 4$, does every drawing of the complete graph $K_n$ have at least
$$\frac14\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}2\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-2}2\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-3}2\right\rfloor$$
crossings?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11136), page 43. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Anchored rectangle packing conjecture
record.statement: For every finite point set $S\subseteq U=[0,1]^2$ with $(0,0)\in S$, where Bob must choose for each $s\in S$ an axis-parallel rectangle $r(s)\subseteq U$ having $s$ as its lower-left corner, with the rectangle interiors pairwise disjoint and with no point of $S$ in the interior of any $r(s)$, can Bob always choose the rectangles so that their total area is at least $\frac12$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11136), page 67. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Integral lattices and embeddings into integer lattices
record.statement: A lattice $L$ in a Euclidean space is called an integral lattice if the inner product $\langle x,y\rangle$ is an integer for every $x,y\in L$. Is every integral lattice $L$ congruent to a sub-lattice of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ for some $n$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11136), page 80. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Bounded monotone paths in convex plane subdivisions with three unbounded rays
record.statement: Is there a constant $c$ such that, for every $n\ge 3$, there is a partition of the plane into convex regions whose boundaries form a connected graph with $n$ vertices and $3$ unbounded rays, such that every monotone path in the graph consists of at most $c$ edges? Here a path is monotone if there is some linear function $\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ that is strictly monotone along the path.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11136), page 81. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Doubly covered paths for coverings by unit discs
record.statement: Is there a constant $c$ such that, for every covering of the plane by closed unit circular discs, any two points situated at distance $d$ from one another and covered by at least two discs can be connected by a path of length at most $\\sqrt{2}d+c$ traveling within the part of the plane covered by at least two discs?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/44](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11136), page 83. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Algebraic K-theory Novikov conjecture for group algebras over Schatten class operators
record.statement: For the ring of Schatten class operators and every group $G$, the associated algebraic $K$-theory assembly map is rationally injective. Consequently, the algebraic $K$-theory Novikov conjecture holds for all group algebras over the ring of Schatten class operators.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/45](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11137), page 20. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Numerical characterization of Du Bois singularities
record.statement: Let $X$ be a proper variety over $\mathbb{C}$ with a fixed basepoint-free linear system $\Delta$. Then $X$ has only Du Bois singularities if and only if $h^i(L,\mathcal{O}_L)\leq f_{0,i}(L)$ for $i>0$ and for every $L\subseteq X$ that is the intersection of general members of $\Delta$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/47](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11139), page 28. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Conservativity of weak intuitionistic constructive set theories over arithmetic
record.statement: For every weak set theory $T$ in question and every arithmetical statement $A$, $T \vdash A \Longleftrightarrow HA + TI(<\lvert T\rvert) \vdash A$, where $TI(<\lvert T\rvert)$ denotes the arithmetical transfinite-induction scheme below the proof-theoretic ordinal of $T$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/52](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11450), page 14. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Universality and polynomial-time solvability of fixed-parameter three-dimensional table integer programs
record.statement:
Consider the integer optimization problem
\[
\min\left\{wx:\ x\in\mathbb Z_{+}^{3\times m\times n},\ \sum_i x_{i,j,k}=a_{j,k},\ \sum_j x_{i,j,k}=b_{i,k},\ \sum_k x_{i,j,k}=c_{i,j}\right\}.
\]
Every integer program can be put precisely into this form; and, for any fixed parameter \(m\), this problem can be solved in polynomial time with variable \(n\).
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11451), page 43. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Boyd–Carr conjecture on the 2-matching/subtour-LP ratio
record.statement: For symmetric traveling-salesman instances whose costs satisfy the triangle inequality, the worst-case ratio of the cost of an optimal 2-matching to the cost of an optimal solution of the subtour linear program is at most $10/9$. Here a 2-matching is an integer solution satisfying the subtour-LP degree and bound constraints, without the subtour-elimination constraints.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11451), page 68. Canonicalized from 5 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Residual-chain approximation for normalized first Betti numbers
record.statement:
For which groups $G$ does the limit
\[
\lim_{i\in I}\frac{b_1(G_i;K)}{[G:G_i]}
\]
exist for all systems $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ with $\bigcap_{i\in I}G_i=\{1\}$ and fields $K$, and is independent of the choice of $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ and $K$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/56](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11454), page 31. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Normalized first Betti numbers in finite-index subgroup systems
record.statement:
For which groups $G$ does the limit
$$
\lim_{i\in I}\frac{b_1(G_i;K)}{[G:G_i]}
$$
exist for every inverse system $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ of normal finite-index subgroups of $G$, directed by inclusion, satisfying $\bigcap_{i\in I}G_i=\{1\}$, and for every field $K$, with the resulting limit independent of both the system $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ and the field $K$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/56](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11454), page 32. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Uniqueness of 7-dimensional regular Riemannian foliations of spheres
record.statement: The report conjectured that there are no 7-dimensional regular Riemannian foliations of spheres other than the Hopf fibration $S^7 \to S^{15} \to S^8$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11568), page 34. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: K-triviality and weak ML-cuppability
record.statement: For every set $A$, $A$ is weakly ML-cuppable if and only if $A$ is not $K$-trivial, where $A$ is weakly ML-cuppable if there is an incomplete Martin-Löf random set $X$ such that $A\oplus X\geq_T\emptyset'.$
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/08](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11575), page 10. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Uniform computation of maximal chains in computable well partial orders
record.statement: There is no hyperarithmetic procedure $f$ such that, for every index $e$ for a computable well partial order $P$, the function $n\mapsto f(e,n)$ is the characteristic function of a maximal chain of $P$. In fact, every such procedure $f$ computes every hyperarithmetic set.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/08](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11575), page 24. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Uniqueness of identifying a mixed-boundary obstacle and its impedance from full far-field data
record.statement:
For the two-dimensional exterior Helmholtz problem described in (1), with 
\(\partial D=\partial D_D\cup\partial D_I\), the boundary components \(\partial D_D\), \(\partial D_I\), and the impedance \(\lambda(x)\) on \(\partial D_I\) are uniquely determined by the far-field data \(u^\infty(\hat x)\) for all measurement points \(\hat x\) and all incident directions \(d\).
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/11](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11578), page 17. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Convergence analysis for the regularized inverse-scattering iteration
record.statement: It is an open problem to extend the convergence analysis to the modification of iteration (10) in which $S$ is replaced by $S_n:=N_{\rho,\alpha_n}\circ R$, where $N_{\rho,\alpha_n}$ is a Tikhonov regularization of the Cauchy operator $N_\rho$ with a null sequence of regularization parameters $\alpha_n$.

record.title: Macdonald polynomials at $t=0$ and normalized $q$-Whittaker functions
record.statement: Conjecture 0.9 asserts that, for every weight $\check\lambda$ under consideration, $$P_{\check\lambda}(q,0,z)=\widehat\Psi_{\check\lambda}(q,z).$$
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/13](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11580), page 14. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Origin of the characteristic length of persistent shear bands
record.statement: For granular materials undergoing shear, what determines the characteristic rolling-correlation length associated with persistent shear bands, whose typical width is about 10–20 particle diameters?

record.title: Conjugacy of maximal invariant 2-subgroups in {2,3}-groups
record.statement: Let $G$ be a ${2,3}$-group whose Sylow $3$-subgroups have exponent $3$. Then, for every element $x\in G$ of order $3$, all maximal $x$-invariant $2$-subgroups of $G$ are conjugate via $C_G(x)$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11583), page 40. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Verification of the inductive conditions for all simple groups and primes
record.statement: Do the inductive McKay and inductive blockwise Alperin weight conditions hold for every simple group and every prime?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11583), page 45. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Non-commutative Waring problem for finite non-abelian simple groups
record.statement: Let $w\in F_d$ be a non-trivial word in the free group on $d$ generators. Then there exists a constant $N=N(w)$ depending on $w$ such that, for every finite non-abelian simple group $G$ with $|G|>N$, one has $w(G)^2=G$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11583), page 48. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Products of two squares in finite quasisimple groups
record.statement: Every element in any finite quasisimple group $G$ is a product of two squares; equivalently, for every $g\in G$, there exist $x,y\in G$ such that $g=x^2y^2$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11583), page 49. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: E10 conjecture for eleven-dimensional supergravity
record.statement: The **E10 conjecture** asserts that the values of all fields of 11-dimensional supergravity and their spatial gradients can be mapped to a null geodesic motion in the infinite-dimensional coset space $E_{10}/K(E_{10})$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/18](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11780), page 11. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Boundedness of continuous cohomology classes for simple Lie groups
record.statement:
For every connected simple Lie group $G$ with finite centre, is the natural comparison map
\[
H^\bullet_{\mathrm{cb}}(G;\mathbb{R})\longrightarrow H^\bullet_{\mathrm{c}}(G;\mathbb{R})
\]
surjective? Equivalently, is every class in $H^\bullet_{\mathrm{c}}(G;\mathbb{R})$ represented by a bounded continuous cocycle?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/18](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11780), page 32. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Rainbow matching conjecture
record.statement: Let $F_1,\\ldots,F_t$ be families of subsets in $\\binom{[n]}{k}$. If $|F_i|>\\max\\left\\{\\binom{n}{k}-\\binom{n-t+1}{k},\\binom{kt-1}{k}\\right\\}$ for every $1\\le i\\le t$, then there is a rainbow matching of size $t$: one that contains exactly one edge from each family.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/19](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11781), page 12. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Elashvili’s index conjecture for coadjoint stabilizers
record.statement: For every $p\in\mathfrak g^*$, $\operatorname{ind}\mathfrak g_p=\operatorname{ind}\mathfrak g$; here $\mathfrak g_p$ denotes the stabilizer of $p$ for the coadjoint action.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/21](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11783), page 10. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Higher-quiver cellular resolution conjecture for consistent toric algebras
record.statement: Conjecture: The statement of Theorem 0.2 holds for every consistent toric algebra of global dimension equal to $n=\dim X$. Namely, the higher quiver $\Delta\subset (S^1)^n$ exists, and the minimal projective $(A,A)$-bimodule resolution of $A$ is the cellular resolution determined by $\Delta$ as in Theorem 0.1.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/21](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11783), page 43. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Classification of toric degenerations of low-degree smooth Fano threefolds
record.statement: All degenerations of smooth Fano threefolds of degree $\leq 12$ in their anticanonical embeddings to Gorenstein toric Fano varieties are completely classified.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/21](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11783), page 55. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Mahler’s conjecture on metric approximation by integer polynomials
record.statement:
For every fixed $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, for almost all real numbers $x$ there are only finitely many polynomials $P\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $\deg P\le n$ such that
\[
|P(x)|<H(P)^{-n-\varepsilon},
\]
where $H(P)=\max_{0\le i\le n}|a_i|$ for $P(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{n}a_i x^i$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/22](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11784), page 32. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Yamabe invariant of cyclic quotients of the 5-sphere
record.statement:
It is conjectured that, for $M=S^5/(\cmathbb{Z}/m)$ with $m\ge 5$, the supremum in the definition of the smooth Yamabe invariant $\sigma(M)$ is attained by the round metric. This would imply
$$
\sigma(M)=\frac{\sigma(S^5)}{m^{2/5}}\approx\frac{78.996}{m^{2/5}}.
$$
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/25](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11787), page 20. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Compactness of the boundary Yamabe problem in dimensions n ≥ 25
record.statement: In analogy with the case without boundary, one wonders whether Theorem 1 is false when $n \ge 25$; namely, whether the stated compactness conclusion for the boundary Yamabe problem can fail in those dimensions.

record.title: Parity theory for knots in arbitrary 3-manifolds
record.statement: Is there any parity theory for knots in arbitrary 3-manifolds?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11790), page 21. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.
